title: How Hormuz crisis is reshaping economic ties between Iraq and Syria
gist: Iraq and Syria agreed free-trade zones at two border crossings, driven chiefly by energy as the Hormuz crisis reshapes regional trade, though analysts question durability given mistrust and instability.

insights.claim: Iraq and Syria agreed to establish major free-trade zones at two border crossings, signalling closer cooperation.
insights.so_what: Overland trade routes gain value while Hormuz is disrupted.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson

insights.claim: Researcher Benjamin Feve says the Iraq-Syria relationship has moved much further than in decades, with energy the biggest driver.
insights.so_what: Energy flows via Syria are a potential export-routing alternative to Hormuz.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson

insights.claim: At the end of September the two customs authorities agreed practical measures for the recently reopened crossings.
insights.so_what: Institutional-level steps make cooperation more durable than political deals.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson

insights.claim: Some question how long cooperation will last given regional instability and longstanding distrust between the current Syrian government and Iraqi counterparts.
insights.so_what: Execution and security risk caveat for any trade or energy corridor thesis.
insights.speaker: Shelly Kittleson
